findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts CHK-002:happy:2 evidence note cites the check 'handler: --alert fires with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=1000 override' (L450-468) as covering 'resolveBurnAlertThresholds with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=500000 returns inputTokens=500000 while other defaults are unchanged', but that check never calls resolveBurnAlertThresholds and never uses 500000 -- it only asserts alert-firing behavior with value 1000. The literal value 500000 does not occur anywhere in usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts or usage-burn-alert.ts (grep confirms zero matches). The only resolver test that overrides LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS to a specific value uses 50000000 (L272-285, 'resolver: each env variable overrides its threshold'), a different untested value. Sibling intents CHK-002:happy:1 (FILE_MB=50->52428800) and CHK-002:happy:3 (AGE_DAYS=14->14) ARE asserted with their exact literal values, so this is a real evidence-note misattribution / coverage gap rather than a stylistic choice.
findings.resolvedReason: Verified fix at commit d3f491966e (usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts L281-285): resolveBurnAlertThresholds is now called with the exact literal LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=500000 and asserts .inputTokens===500000, matching CHK-002:happy:2 literally. Ran usage-burn-alert-smoke.js directly (21 checks, all pass) to confirm.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts CHK-003:edge:4 requires a session that trips ALL THREE reasons (file-size + input-tokens + session-age) and lists all three in its warning line; no such fixture exists anywhere in the smoke. The only multi-reason fixture (codex-burn-A/HOT, integration check L372-374) is explicitly asserted via assert.deepEqual([...hot.reasons].sort(), ["input-tokens","session-age"], ...) to trip EXACTLY two reasons, never file-size (its transcript is a few hundred bytes, well under the 100MB default). The renderers check (L435-447) constructs a single-reason (input-tokens only) fixture. Evidence notes both for CHK-003:edge:4 ("integration: HOT trips multiple reasons listed together; renderers list reasons joined") and for CHK-001:happy:5 ("evaluator per-reason isolation + edge: all-three-reasons session (doctor fixture)") misdescribe this as a 3-reason test -- there is no 3-reason (doctor) fixture in the file. renderBurnFindingBlock's reasons.join(...) line (core/usage-burn-alert.ts ~L250) is therefore untested with 3 simultaneous reasons.
findings.resolvedReason: Verified fix at commit d3f491966e (usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts L448-475): a new check now asserts a 3-reason (file-size+input-tokens+session-age) finding both at evaluator level and via the real doctor handler (FILE_MB=0.0001 makes the HOT fixture trip file-size too). JSON-level assertion binds to sessionId===codex-burn-A correctly. Ran usage-burn-alert-smoke.js directly (21 checks, all pass) to confirm. Filed a separate low-severity finding F-004 for a latent (currently-harmless) line-selection bug in the same check's text-mode assertion.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts CHK-001:edge:3 requires "A codex session with inputTokens=0 and a claude session with all-zero usage fields are not flagged for input-tokens", but no fixture in the smoke uses a zero-valued codex usage() or an all-zero claude usage object. The nearest row (L352, sessionId 'bbb') has cacheReadInputTokens:2000 (nonzero) and IS flagged, not an example of the intended not-flagged-at-zero case. Existing tests only cover near-threshold (1000) and clearly nonzero (2000/4300/5000/150000000) values. grep across the file confirms no codexUsage(0) call and no all-zero claude usage object anywhere. The evidence note title ("evaluator: zero-usage rows below strictly-greater thresholds are not flagged") does not correspond to any check in the file.
findings.resolvedReason: Verified fix at commit d3f491966e (usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts L345-353): explicit zero-usage fixtures added -- codex codexUsage(0) and claude all-zero four-field usage -- both asserted to produce zero findings, with fileSizeOf and firstTimestamp controlled so only the input-tokens invariant is exercised. Ran usage-burn-alert-smoke.js directly (21 checks, all pass) to confirm.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/usage-burn-alert-smoke.ts L468 (the new F-002-fix check 'doctor: a session tripping file-size + input-tokens + session-age lists all three reasons', covering CHK-003:edge:4): the hotLine selector `text.split("\n").find((line) => line.includes("tripped:") && text.includes("codex-burn-A"))` references the OUTER `text` variable in its second predicate instead of `line`. Since `text` (the whole doctor output) always contains the substring 'codex-burn-A' somewhere, this second condition is vacuously true and the selector actually just grabs the FIRST line anywhere in the doctor output containing 'tripped:', not specifically codex-burn-A's warning line. Empirically confirmed (ran the same fixture setup standalone): with FILE_MB=0.0001 the doctor output contains THREE 'tripped:' lines -- one for codex-burn-A (file-size, input-tokens, session-age) and two file-size-only lines for codex-at-C and codex-ok-B (also swept up by the tiny threshold). The assertion currently passes only because evaluateBurnAlerts sorts findings by burnInputTokens descending (core/usage-burn-alert.ts L216-221), so codex-burn-A (150M tokens) happens to render first among the three -- i.e. it works by coincidence of fixture/sort ordering, not because the code actually identifies codex-burn-A's line. CHK-003:edge:4 requires proving that the specific tripped session's warning line lists all three reasons; a selector that cannot actually bind to a named session does not reliably verify that claim and would silently start checking the wrong line if the fixture set or sort order ever changes (e.g. a future fixture with higher burnInputTokens added before HOT, or HOT's own burn value lowered). Fix: change `text.includes("codex-burn-A")` to `line.includes("codex-burn-A")`.
